answer:
**Verdict:** Low federal anti-hacking risk if *100% logged-out*; existential civil risk if any login, fake account, or extension touches LinkedIn; active statutory exposure under state data-broker laws (esp. CA) & right-of-publicity class actions if profiles appear in marketing/previews.

### Exposure by Vector

*   **CFAA (Anti-Hacking) — Low (if logged-out):** *hiQ v. LinkedIn* (9th Cir. 2022) held scraping public, non-authenticated pages isn't "unauthorized access". Risk spikes sharply if bypassing auth walls, using stolen/fake credentials, or circumventing technical gates (CFAA / DMCA §1201).
*   **LinkedIn Civil Suit (Contract / Fraud / Injunction) — Existential if logged-in, Gray if logged-out:**
    *   *Logged-out only:* Strong defense under *Meta v. Bright Data* (N.D. Cal. 2024: ToS doesn't bind logged-out scraping) & *X v. Bright Data* (N.D. Cal. 2024: Copyright Act §301 preempts contract/tort claims over copying public content). **Caveat:** District-court rulings only (non-binding outside N.D. Cal; *X v. Bright Data* remains in litigation) — Microsoft/LinkedIn can still outspend you into settlement.
    *   *Logged-in, extensions, or fake-account farms:* Fatal. User Agreement §8.2 binds account holders (*hiQ* ended in a $500K consent judgment + permanent injunction + data destruction on contract grounds). LinkedIn actively kills commercial enrichment scrapers using fake accounts: shut down Proxycurl (*LinkedIn v. Nubela*, Jul 2025) & ProAPIs/Netswift (*LinkedIn v. ProAPIs*, Sep 2026 consent judgment: permanent ban + delete all data, reports, & code). Also nukes company pages/accounts (Apollo.io, Seamless.AI, HeyReach) & scans client-side extensions.
    *   *3rd-party scraping APIs:* You inherit sudden outage risk (Proxycurl died overnight) + potential inducement/tortious-interference exposure if your vendor uses fake accounts.
*   **Data Broker & State Privacy Laws — High & Actively Enforced:**
    *   *Data broker registration:* Selling enriched people data w/o a direct consumer relationship triggers broker registration in **CA, TX, OR, VT**.
    *   *CA Delete Act (SB 362 / DROP):* Deletion processing via CalPrivacy's DROP portal became mandatory Aug 1, 2026 (every 45 days; tightens to **30 days** Jan 1, 2027 via AB 883). Fines: **$200/day** per unregistered day or unfulfilled request (CalPrivacy hit LocateSmarter w/ $116K fine in Aug 2026). Mandatory 3rd-party audits start 2028.
    *   *CCPA/CPRA + ~20 state privacy laws:* CA's B2B exemption is dead. CCPA applies if >$26.625M revenue, ≥100K CA consumers bought/sold/shared/yr, or ≥50% revenue from selling/sharing PI. **Don't rely blindly on the "publicly available" carve-out:** fails for data restricted to logged-in LinkedIn members, inferred/appended non-public fields (emails, phones), & narrows further under CA SB 923 (eff. Jan 1, 2027, extending deletion to 3rd-party-sourced PI).
*   **Right of Publicity Class Actions — High if Public-Facing, Low if Private:** ZoomInfo paid **$29.6M** (2024 settlement: CA, IL, IN, NV) & faces follow-on WA suits for showing scraped profiles on public SEO teaser/preview pages to sell subscriptions. Minimal risk if enriched data stays strictly inside paying customers' private CRMs & never promotes your product.
*   **Copyright, Biometrics & Customer MSAs:**
    *   Facts (name, title, employer, dates) aren't copyrightable; narrative bios, posts, & headshots are. Never run facial recognition on headshots (IL BIPA / TX CUBI = massive statutory damages).
    *   Enterprise buyers demand data-provenance warranties & uncapped IP/privacy indemnities; scraping breaches standard "compliant w/ all 3rd-party terms" reps.

### What to Do Now

1.  **Hard wall on logged-out only:** Zero company, employee, customer, or burner accounts; zero Chrome extensions. If using a data vendor, audit collection methods & require written warranty against logged-in/fake-account scraping.
2.  **Scrape facts only:** Pull name, title, company, work dates; drop photos, posts, & long-form bios.
3.  **Zero public teasers:** Never publish scraped profiles on SEO landing pages, ads, or unauthenticated free-trial previews.
4.  **Check broker thresholds immediately:** If selling enriched profiles at scale (esp. ≥100K CA records or ≥50% revenue from data sales), register in CA/TX/OR/VT & wire up CA DROP suppression.
5.  **Scrub LinkedIn marks:** Remove "LinkedIn" from product names/ads — LinkedIn stacks Lanham Act trademark claims onto scraping suits.
6.  **Fix customer MSAs:** Carve out 3rd-party ToS compliance warranties, cap liability, & keep customer CRM enrichment strictly behind auth.
